mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate has a negative effect on equity returns; therefore, the current rate of 1.7% (which is below 2.0%) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days due to reduced discount rates for equity cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month rise in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) signals inconsistent monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days due to equity market volatility.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The housing starts series (HOUST) has a negative effect on equity returns; therefore, the current value of 1287.0 (which is below 1300) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days due to reduced construction activity signaling monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 1300, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days due to improved consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls below 3.5% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low industrial production (INDPRO < 105) and low housing starts (HOUST < 1300) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days due to increased recession risk.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105 AND HOUST < 1300, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP growth above 2.0% QoQ and CPIAUCSL YoY above 2.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over 60 trading days due to increased risk of monetary tightening and equity market correction.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 QoQ > 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
